reason: Water loss should change the blood sample and begin the water-saving sequence.

reason: The brain water sensors should detect the increased concentration and start the water-saving response.

expectation: ADH will increase water recovery from the collecting ducts.

effect: ADH increased collecting-duct water recovery, completing the first goal. The remaining pieces suggest building the hormone-release route into the body.
reaction: The water-channel and concentration difference make the kidney response clearer.
reason: The hormone-releasing nerve endings and pituitary blood vessels are shown alongside each other, suggesting a route for ADH to enter blood.
expectation: This will form a connection through which the nerve endings release hormone into the blood.

effect: The nerve endings and vessels formed a brain-to-blood hormone route, ready to connect to the body.
reaction: The route makes the link between nerve signalling and a blood-borne hormone clearer.
reason: The remaining goal calls for giving the body a water-control route, so the new route should connect to the body.
expectation: The body will gain a connection from brain water sensors to the kidneys via the blood.

effect: The body now has a bloodborne water-control route to the kidneys; it still needs a drink.
reaction: The route connects the earlier hormone example to the body model.
reason: Drinking water is the remaining visible piece for replacing water losses.
expectation: The body will take in water to help replace its losses.

effect: Drinking water entered the circulation, and the planned comparison showed ADH signalling decreasing as plasma concentration approached its usual range. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback connection is satisfying, though the picture plan rather than finished artwork carries much of the explanation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting ADH to collecting-duct water recovery was most worthwhile: the planned channels, concentration difference and return to blood give a concrete mechanism for conserving water.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the already-built hormone route to the body was predictable and added little explanation beyond its integration into the model.

surprise.text: The final comparison made the feedback clearer: as plasma concentration approaches its usual range after drinking, fewer ADH signals leave the pituitary.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but the initial sensor-to-hormone result introduced ADH without spelling out its name, leaving an important term unexplained for this audience.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the sensor, hormone and kidney sequence connected familiar diffusion ideas to regulation, although I would want unfamiliar terms explained more fully.
